title: Federal appraisal threshold for commercial real estate loans: $500,000
rule: Institutions regulated by the OCC, the Federal Reserve and the FDIC need an appraisal by a state certified or licensed appraiser for real estate-related financial transactions, with exceptions. A commercial real estate transaction of $500,000 or less is excepted; the institution obtains an evaluation instead. Above $500,000, a commercial real estate transaction needs a state certified appraiser. Commercial means not secured by a single one-to-four family residence, so multifamily counts; for a loan, transaction value is the loan amount.

citation.authority: 12 CFR 34.42, 34.43(a)(13), (b) and (d)(2); 12 CFR 225.63; 12 CFR 323.3 (implementing title XI of FIRREA)

changeWatch: A joint rule by the OCC, Federal Reserve and FDIC changing the appraisal thresholds; 12 CFR 34.43 was last amended in 2019.
